items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: My bass player, in that band, was named Harry Gray

ctx.x: Well, during that time we would play dance music, and it would give the people a chance to dance, and sometimes we'd have some nice dancers, even, just from our guests that were there, you know. ^ Had some fun. They'd do all this swing, and a lot of them would do the twist and all that stuff. I think I would like to inject one thing while we're talking about that band. This is an important fellah. My bass player, in that band, was named Harry Gray, G-R-A-Y, whom we campaigned, and almost had to fight to run for…

bass, and he was always a figurehead. He was a good man. I used to have him pay the fellows off, you know, and keep books and all this sort of stuff, and he was a good figurehead. He was pretty accurate, and he was a well-to-do man, and we campaigned for him, and he won the presidency in Chicago, and he did an awful lot there. Naturally, I had to get another bass player, and the bass player that followed him was a guy named Jesse Simpkins. He was an excellent bassist, and he was from my home town. He was a little…
